title: Scripture and Prayer
definition: Scripture and Prayer means God’s Word shapes how believers speak to God, trust His promises, confess sin, and seek His will.
summary: Scripture and Prayer means God’s Word shapes how believers speak to God, trust His promises, confess sin, and seek His will.
christFocus: Jesus prayed according to the Father’s will, taught His disciples to pray, and gives believers access to God through His finished work.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture teaches believers how to pray. It gives words for praise, confession, lament, thanksgiving, intercession, repentance, surrender, and hope. Prayer becomes stronger when shaped by what God has spoken.

The Bible also corrects prayer. It moves believers away from selfish demands, empty repetition, fear, and unbelief. Scripture teaches us to seek God’s will, trust His character, and pray with honesty rather than performance.

Christ brings believers near to the Father, and the Holy Spirit helps them pray. Scripture and prayer belong together because God’s Word teaches us who God is, and prayer responds to Him in faith.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people feel they do not know how to pray, especially when they are ashamed, grieving, tempted, or spiritually tired. Scripture gives language for the heart when words feel weak.

This doctrine also protects prayer from becoming detached from truth. Prayer is not wishful thinking; it is communion with the God who has revealed Himself in His Word.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let Scripture guide your prayers. Turn a verse into praise, confession, request, or surrender. When you do not know what to say, begin with God’s Word and trust the Holy Spirit to help you pray honestly through Christ.
